_meta.what: What stands out box, up to 3 items per country page
_meta.picked_by: TLS Youth; entry tests in youth/SPEC.md (D-351, D-354)

items.text: of 16-26s said in 2024 that people like them are well represented in parliament, down from 63% in 2019.
items.against: 32% in autumn 2025, about level with all ages (31%). Early waves had about 300 people.
items.source: Foresight Research for the Austrian Parliament, Junge Menschen und Demokratie 2025

items.text: of 16-34s look at the next twelve months with confidence, and 19% with worry.
items.against: Over-60s: 24% confidence, 40% worry. Here the young are the less worried group.
items.source: IMAS, face to face, Jan to Mar 2026, 3,052 people

items.text: of Flemish 18-24s name heavy pressure to perform as a reason they don't feel good in society.
items.against: Against 3% of over-65s, same survey. 27% name loneliness, against 9%.
items.source: VRT, Foto van Vlaanderen, Nov to Dec 2025, 180 people aged 18-24

items.text: of French-speaking 15-year-old girls felt lonely most of the time or always, against 12% of boys.
items.against: A 25-point gap, the widest of 44 countries and regions in the survey.
items.source: HBSC school survey 2021/22, WHO Europe

items.text: of Flemish 18-24s say they are worried about the presence of Islam.
items.against: Against 67% of over-65s, same survey.
items.source: VRT, Foto van Vlaanderen, Nov to Dec 2025, 2,261 people aged 12+

items.text: out of 10: life satisfaction of over-65s, the lowest of 36 countries in Eurostat's table.
items.against: 16-29s are at 7.1. A gap of 1.6 points, against 0.5 in the EU.
items.source: Eurostat, ilc_pw01, 2024

items.text: of under-30s believe their own behaviour can make a difference to the climate.
items.against: Against 42% of over-65s, same survey. The gap is mostly low over-65s.
items.source: EIB Climate Survey with BVA, Aug 2022

items.text: out of 10: trust in other people among 16-29s, the lowest in the EU.
items.against: EU 6.0. Over-65s are lowest too, so this is the whole country, not only the young.
items.source: Eurostat, ilc_pw03, 2025

items.text: of 18-24 voters chose ANO, the party that won the October 2025 election.
items.against: Against 54% of 65-74s. The young went mostly to the outgoing coalition.
items.source: Joint post-election study of six agencies, Oct to Nov 2025, 7,738 adults

items.text: of under-30s are satisfied with Czech membership of the EU.
items.against: Against 57% of 55-64s, same poll. Every age group has a satisfied majority.
items.source: CVVM, Aug 2025, 1,640 people aged 15+

items.text: of 20-29s want Ukraine to keep fighting with no concessions.
items.against: Against 32% of everyone aged 15 and over, same poll.
items.source: CVVM, Oct to Nov 2025, 1,061 people aged 15+

items.text: of under-35s want the Bundeswehr to be part of a European army.
items.against: Against 61% of those 35 and over, the reverse of the usual assumption.
items.source: Deutschland-Monitor 2025, forsa by telephone, Apr to May 2025, 4,005 people aged 16+

items.text: of 18-29s say pensioners should get tax cuts when workers do.
items.against: Against 89% of over-65s. The questions were written with the pensioners' organisation.
items.source: Epinion for Ældre Sagen, Mar 2026, 2,017 adults

items.text: of young men think nuclear power would be a good idea for Denmark, against 33% of young women.
items.against: Ages 18-29. No figure for older Danes.
items.source: Voxmeter for DUF, Mar 2026, 1,065 people aged 18-29

items.text: of 20-29s would try to leave Estonia if it were attacked.
items.against: Against 9% of 60-74s. The same shape in 2025 and 2024.
items.source: Kantar Emor for the Ministry of Defence, Mar 2026

items.text: of 18-24s voted in the 2023 parliamentary election.
items.against: Against 74% of 65-74s.
items.source: National Electoral Committee, Riigikogu election, Mar 2023

items.text: of 15-24s in the labour force were unemployed in 2025, more than in France (20%).
items.against: EU 15%. Up from 17% in 2023.
items.source: Eurostat, une_rt_a, 2025

items.text: of 16-26s say the political system works so badly that only radical change can fix it.
items.against: The highest of seven countries; next is Italy, at 26%.
items.source: TUI Stiftung, YouGov online panel, Apr to May 2026, 507 people aged 16-26

items.text: of 16-26s call democracy the best form of state, down from 70% in 2022.
items.against: Same survey. Germany fell from 63% to 53%, Spain from 62% to 49%.
items.source: TUI Stiftung, YouGov online panel, 2022 and 2026

items.text: of 16-26s plan to work mainly in Greece over the next five years, the lowest of seven countries.
items.against: Italy 40%; the six EU countries average 48%. A plan, not a move.
items.source: TUI Stiftung, YouGov online panel, Apr to May 2026, 507 people aged 16-26

items.text: of Gen Z (18-28) say democracy is preferable to any other form of government.
items.against: Against 84% of the oldest generations. 24% of Gen Z say authoritarian rule can be preferable in some circumstances.
items.source: 40dB for El País and Cadena SER, Nov 2025, 2,000 people

items.text: of women aged 15-29 call themselves feminist, down from 67% in 2021.
items.against: Young men moved from 33% to 26%.
items.source: Barómetro Juventud y Género 2025, 1,528 people aged 15-29

items.text: of 18-24s feel unwanted loneliness.
items.against: Against 15% of 65-74s, same survey.
items.source: Fundación ONCE and Fundación AXA, SoledadES, 2024

items.text: of 15-24s say Finns should defend themselves by arms in all situations, and 30% can't say.
items.against: Against 83% of over-50s, same survey.
items.source: MTS, Sep to Oct 2025, 1,072 people aged 15+

items.text: of girls aged about 14-16 report moderate or severe anxiety, against 9% of boys.
items.against: Self-reported symptoms, not diagnoses.
items.source: THL, School Health Promotion study, spring 2025

items.text: of 18-34s pick "benefit seniors more than the young", from three options on public policy.
items.against: Against 32% of over-65s, same poll. Asked during the protests, after a text on the blockades.
items.source: Cluster17 for L'Opinion, 7-9 Oct 2026, 1,271 adults

items.text: of 18-24s support the school pupils' movement or have sympathy for it, 50% outright.
items.against: Against 42% of those 35 and over, same poll. About 100 people aged 18-24.
items.source: Ifop for LCI, 6-7 Oct 2026, 1,000 adults

items.text: of 18-24s favour weighting votes by age, so the young count for more and the old for less.
items.against: Against 3% of 65-74s and 4% of over-75s, same poll. A majority is against at every age.
items.source: Cluster17 for Marianne, 25-28 Jun 2025, 1,340 adults

items.text: of 14-year-old pupils trust the national government, the second lowest of 20 countries.
items.against: Survey average 53%. Only Poland is lower, at 27%.
items.source: ICCS 2022, 2,766 pupils in Croatia

items.text: of over-65s are at risk of poverty, against 11% of 16-29s.
items.against: The widest gap in the EU against the old. EU: 16% and 19%.
items.source: Eurostat, ilc_li02, 2025

items.text: of under-30s backed Fidesz before the April 2026 election.
items.against: Against 50% of over-65s, same poll. Tisza had 65% of the young.
items.source: 21 Kutatóközpont, reported by Telex, Mar 2026

items.text: of the youngest voters trust politicians, and 61% distrust them.
items.against: Against 68% trust among over-65s, same exit poll.
items.source: Ipsos B&A exit poll, Nov 2024, 5,018 voters

items.text: of 18-24s say their generation has more opportunities than their parents had.
items.against: Against 76% of over-65s. Still above young people in Sweden (28%), Italy (17%) and Spain (12%).
items.source: RED C, WIN survey, Jan 2026, 1,013 adults

items.text: of women aged 18-24 are very worried about climate change, against 36% of young men.
items.against: Among all adults the gap is 8 points.
items.source: EPA and Yale, Climate Change in the Irish Mind, 2021, 4,000 adults

items.text: of 15-24s support the EU aim of climate neutrality by 2050.
items.against: Against 61% of over-55s, the widest gap in the EU. EU: 86% and 79%.
items.source: Special Eurobarometer 565, Feb to Mar 2025

items.text: of 15-24s are satisfied with how democracy works in the EU.
items.against: Against 58% of over-55s. The same in 2025.
items.source: Standard Eurobarometer, Mar 2026

items.text: of young women fear an outbreak of war in Europe, against 72% of young men.
items.against: Ages 12-29. Gaps of 15 to 22 points on war, climate, terror and violence.
items.source: Youth Survey Luxembourg 2024, University of Luxembourg

items.text: of 15-24s expect their household's finances to improve over the next year.
items.against: Against 10% of over-55s, the widest gap in the EU. EU young: 31%.
items.source: Standard Eurobarometer, Mar 2026

items.text: of 15-24s are satisfied with how democracy works in the EU.
items.against: Against 52% of over-55s. The same in 2025.
items.source: Standard Eurobarometer, Mar 2026

items.text: of over-65s are at risk of poverty, the highest in the EU.
items.against: Against 16% of 16-29s. EU over-65s: 16%.
items.source: Eurostat, ilc_li02, 2025

items.text: of 16-35s favour allowing abortion in some form, the only age group with a majority.
items.against: 86% of pensioners are against it in all circumstances.
items.source: MaltaToday, Jul 2022, 652 people

items.text: of 18-34s say people like them are disadvantaged in finding a home.
items.against: Against 22% of over-55s. No such age gap on jobs, judges or political representation.
items.source: SCP, LISS panel, Apr 2026, about 1,240 adults

items.text: of 18-24s trust politics, and 62% of 15-17s.
items.against: Against 31% of 65-74s, the reverse of the usual pattern.

items.text: of 18-24s worry a lot about their financial future.
items.against: Against 19% of 65-74s.
items.source: CBS, wellbeing statistics, 2025

items.text: of Polish 16-26s expect to do better than their parents, and 28% worse. No other country asked has more better than worse.
items.against: Elsewhere, 21-29% better and 47-66% worse. Same survey, seven countries.
items.source: TUI Stiftung, YouGov online panel, 24 Apr to 21 May 2026

items.text: of Polish 16-26s rate the country's economy as bad, down from 59% in 2023.
items.against: The largest move of the seven countries. The next lowest in 2026 is Spain, at 40%.
items.source: TUI Stiftung, surveys of 2023 and 2026

items.text: of boys in their final school year call their views right-wing, up from 19% in 2021.
items.against: Against 11% of girls. Part of the rise is boys who used to decline the question.
items.source: CBOS for KCPU, Nov 2025, 1,506 pupils

items.text: of 18-24 voters chose PS in the 2025 election.
items.against: Against 40% of over-65 voters. Chega peaks at 35-44 (33%), not among the youngest (25%).
items.source: CESOP-Católica exit poll for RTP, May 2025

items.text: of 15-24s call climate change a very serious problem.
items.against: Against 43% of 40-54s. The second widest gap of 27 countries; EU 6 points.
items.source: Special Eurobarometer 565, Feb to Mar 2025

items.text: of women aged 15-29 are not in work, education or training, the highest in the EU.
items.against: EU 12%. Young Romanian men: 14%.
items.source: Eurostat, edat_lfse_20, 2025

items.text: of 18-29s who name a party back PSD.
items.against: Against 38% of over-60s. 16% back SENS, a party outside parliament.
items.source: INSCOP for Informat.ro, Oct to Nov 2025, 3,000 adults

items.text: of 16-29s rate their mental health good.
items.against: Against 78% of 30-74s. Physical health differs much less (64% and 70%).
items.source: MUCF, 2024

items.text: of 16-29s rate their trust in other people at 7 or more out of 10.
items.against: Against 59% of 30-74s, and 30% among 16-19s.
items.source: MUCF, 2024

items.text: of 16-29s say conscription should be compulsory.
items.against: Against 52% of 30-74s.
items.source: MUCF, 2024

items.text: net trust in the speaker of parliament among Gen Z, born after 1995.
items.against: Boomers: +19. The gap is about the government of the day; opposition parties show little age gap.
items.source: Valicon, Oct 2025, 1,096 adults, reported by STA

items.text: of 14-29s call a university degree very important, down from 77% in 2018.
items.against: The largest drop of any value in the study.
items.source: FES Youth Study Slovenia 2024, 602 people aged 14-29

items.text: of 18-24 voters chose Gibanje Svoboda in March 2026.
items.against: Against 42% of over-65s. The young spread across smaller parties, left and right.
items.source: Mediana exit poll for POP TV and RTV Slovenija, Mar 2026

items.text: of 15-24s are satisfied with how democracy works in the EU, the highest share in the EU.
items.against: Against 43% of over-55s. Slovaks aged 25-39 are as positive as the young.
items.source: Standard Eurobarometer, Mar 2026

items.text: of 18-30s who name a party back Progresívne Slovensko.
items.against: Against about 21% of all voters. The governing Smer has 5.5% of the young.
items.source: Focus for Aktuality.sk, Jul to Oct 2025

items.text: of 18-24s support a year of compulsory military service, and 78% oppose it.
items.against: Over-65s are split, 46% to 46%.
items.source: YouGov, Sep 2023

items.text: of women aged 18-27 say Britain is a racist country, against 37% of men.
items.against: Gaps of 18 to 21 points on pride, racism and tolerance. No older comparison.
items.source: YouGov for The Times, Sep to Oct 2024
